blocks.content: The Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992 came into force on June 1, 1993, constitutionalising urban local government.

rows: State Legislature Act (or Parliament Act for UTs)

items: Distinguish between functional items: The 12th Schedule (Municipalities) contains 18 functions, whereas the 11th Schedule (Panchayats) contains 29 functions.
Cantonment Boards are created and administered directly by the Central Government under the Ministry of Defence, not by state enactments.
In Metropolitan Planning Committees (MPC), at least two-thirds of members must be elected by elected members of the municipalities and chairpersons of the Panchayats in the metropolitan area.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 accorded constitutional status to urban local bodies in India.
The Act provides for three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas, Municipal Council for smaller urban areas, and Municipal Corporation for larger urban areas.
Mandates direct elections for all members of a municipality, with seats reserved for SCs, STs, and not less than one-third for women.
Fixed tenure of 5 years for every municipality, with elections required within 6 months of dissolution.
Constitutes District Planning Committees (Article 243-ZD) and Metropolitan Planning Committees (Article 243-ZE) to consolidate draft development plans.
